properties.name: Crossing of the Bavispe
properties.reasoning: The book names no crossing point. The Bavispe runs south along the eastern foot of the Sierra La Madera past Villa Hidalgo, Huásabas and Granados, so a wolf leaving the eastern slopes crosses it there; the point is on INEGI's channel of the river, and the area runs along it towards Granados and Villa Hidalgo. The Bavispe is one river bent into a long U: it flows north past Bacerac, turns west at Colonia Morelos and comes back south here. So her way north to the line at 108°30′ W must cross it a second time, on the eastern arm, which the book does not mention.
properties.outline_rule: On the river: the Bavispe's channel (the highest-order INEGI stream in the circle, its main stem) and 1.5 km either side. She crosses the river, so the crossing is on it; where along this reach is still open, so the whole reach in the circle stays.

properties.name: Between Clanton and Foster draws
properties.reasoning: The high country between Clanton Draw (GNIS 887634) and Foster Draw (GNIS 889164), which lie 3 km apart.
properties.outline_rule: The ground between the two draws: the strip between lines through the GNIS points of Clanton Draw and Foster Draw that run down the general slope of the circle (the way the draws run), with 400 m beyond each. NHD does not name the draws' channels here.

properties.name: Cloverdale Creek (the trap)
properties.reasoning: Where the trap was set: the vaqueros' noon fire, off the Cloverdale Creek road. In episode 1-08 Billy rides out of Cloverdale at dawn, turns west up the creek road and leaves it about two hours later to cross a pasture to the fire. At a horse's walk that is some 8 to 12 km. In Census TIGER 2023 the road follows the creek for 7 km from Cloverdale, to where Co Rd C106 branches west, and ends 9.6 km out; the point is on the road 8 km from Cloverdale and the area covers its upper reach and the pastures either side. The GNIS point for Cloverdale Creek (887693) lies downstream, east of Cloverdale, which the ride west rules out.

properties.name: Cloverdale Creek road
properties.reasoning: The same trap site as the wolf's last stop (J1, stop 13; the reasoning is there): about two hours' ride west up the creek road from Cloverdale.

properties.name: Robertson's crossfence
properties.reasoning: On the creek road: leading the wolf back down it, Billy stops at the crossfence after an hour, with Cloverdale an hour's ride further on, so about halfway, 4 km from Cloverdale by the road (Census TIGER 2023). From there he turns south across open country. The Robertson family ran the Cloverdale Ranch from the early 1900s (Range Magazine, winter 2000, rangemagazine.com/archives/stories/winter00/bootheel.htm), so the fence is likely theirs. GNIS has no Robertson ranch; the area covers the stretch of road the halfway estimate could miss by.
properties.outline_rule: On the creek road he leads the wolf down (1-08): within 500 m of the Cloverdale Creek road (Census TIGER 2023, Cloverdale Rd C001, Co Rd C001 and Co Rd C106). The circle says where along the road.

properties.name: Ranch house on the volcanic plain
properties.reasoning: Past the Guadalupe pass and before the boundary. The book crosses a broad volcanic plain here. The Geronimo–San Bernardino volcanic field covers the northern San Bernardino Valley in basalt, from Cochise County into Hidalgo County and Sonora (New Mexico Geological Society guidebook; Arizona Geological Survey), which is the ground south-west of the pass. The ranch house itself is unnamed.
properties.outline_rule: The plain: ground with a slope under 3 degrees (smoothed 30 m DEM) north of the boundary at 31°20′ N, the part joined to the stop. The ranch is on the broad volcanic plain before the boundary.

properties.name: The boundary, a monument in sight
properties.reasoning: Boundary monuments stand along 31°20′ N here. The area covers the stretch south of the volcanic plain and north of the Cajon Bonita.
properties.outline_rule: Within 3 km of the boundary along 31°20′ N, where the monuments stand: they are at the line with a monument in sight.

properties.name: The mud-house settlement
properties.reasoning: Unnamed. Between the crossing at Colonia Oaxaca and Colonia Morelos. The pin is on the Bavispe's valley floor, the ground the area is drawn on.
properties.outline_rule: The Bavispe's valley floor: ground within 4 km of the river and no more than 60 m above it. They ride down the river path, across a meadow to a road and south along it to the settlement (1-09).

properties.name: The hacienda
properties.reasoning: Unnamed in the book. The text sets it on flat ground beside the Batopito River, with the road on the other side (1-10): the Batepito stream near Colonia Morelos (GeoNames 4017287), 1.7 km from the estimate. The area is bounded by the reach within a day of Morelos and the Pilares Teras. Bell 2000 (p. 107) also puts the hacienda on this river.
properties.outline_rule: Flat ground beside the Batepito: within 2 km of the river (INEGI streams along Natural Earth's Río Batepito), no more than 30 m above it, with a slope under 5 degrees. The book has the road on the other bank, but not which bank that is.

properties.name: A promontory above the Bavispe
properties.reasoning: Two days later, from a promontory, he sees the Bavispe seeming to flow the wrong way and realises that his ride has brought him back over the range to the reach where the river flows north, east of the Sierras. That north-running reach is the upper Bavispe between Bacerac and Bavispe town, so the promontory is on the sierra's eastern edge above it; the area covers that edge.
properties.outline_rule: A promontory over the north-running Bavispe on the sierra's side: ground west of the river (its main stem in INEGI), at least 150 m above it and within 8 km of it.

properties.name: Among the Indians in the Sierras
properties.reasoning: He wanders the high country for weeks and Indians feed him; the book names no range or camp. The area covers the Sierra El Tigre country south of the mining town and west of the upper Bavispe, between his stop at El Tigre and his descent to the river.
properties.outline_rule: The high country: ground above 1,500 m west of the upper Bavispe (west of the line Bacerac to Bavispe, extended). The book names no range, so this only drops the valleys.

properties.name: The eastern escarpment above the Bavispe barranca
properties.reasoning: From the eastern escarpment he looks east over the Bavispe's barranca to the Carretas Plain beyond, then goes down, sleeps by the river and rides north along the river track to a ford. So the escarpment is on the sierra's eastern edge upriver (south) of Huisiachepic; the area is set south-west of the Huisiachepic estimate.
properties.outline_rule: The escarpment's edge: ground that looks down at least 300 m within 6 km to the east, on the west side of the upper Bavispe (its main stem in INEGI) and within 8 km of it. He looks east over the barranca and then goes down to the river.

properties.name: Huisiachepic, the heretic's town
properties.reasoning: No gazetteer or source has Huisiachepic (see docs/open-questions.md). The text puts it across a ford on the upper Bavispe, reached by riding north along the river, and several days upriver (south) of Tamichopa. The pin is on the upper Bavispe's main stem (INEGI), at the point of the river nearest the midpoint of the reach between Mesa Tres Ríos and Huachinera; that midpoint is 28.2 km straight-line south of Tamichopa.
properties.outline_rule: The river town: ground within 1.5 km of the upper Bavispe (the circle's main stem in INEGI) and no more than 150 m above it, so benches above the canyon floor stay. The town is across a ford on the river; which bank is not known.

properties.name: A pass in the Guadalupes on the old Cloverdale road
properties.reasoning: He rides the old road from Douglas to Cloverdale all day and crosses a cold pass in the Guadalupe Mountains, with old names carved in the rock, and looks down on the Animas Plain at dusk. The book does not name the pass; the area is where a road east from Douglas toward Cloverdale crosses the range, north of the low pass of J2. The pin is by the road over the range (Geronimo Trail in Census TIGER 2023), which the area follows.
properties.outline_rule: On the road over the range: within 1.5 km of the Douglas to Cloverdale roads (Geronimo Trail and Cloverdale Road in Census TIGER).

properties.name: Sanders' (the SK Bar)
properties.reasoning: Old man Sanders and Leona tell him what happened. No source names an SK Bar ranch (see docs/open-questions.md); the text puts it nine miles north of the Parham house by road, so the estimate is about 14.5 km north of Cloverdale.
properties.outline_rule: The ranch house is on the road: within 2.5 km of the road north from Cloverdale (today's State Highway 338 and Cloverdale Road, Census TIGER). The book gives nine miles by road from the Parham house, so the circle still fixes where along the road.

properties.name: The Websters' (Boyd)
properties.reasoning: Boyd is lodging with the Websters on the east side of Lordsburg; the book gives no street. The area covers the east side of town.
properties.outline_rule: The east side of Lordsburg: the town's streets (within 250 m of Census TIGER local streets) east of the town's centre point. Today's town is larger than the town of the 1940s.

properties.name: Leaving the Websters', Lordsburg
properties.reasoning: The brothers leave the Websters' with the shotgun, money and food, and cross the Southern Pacific tracks out of Lordsburg.
properties.outline_rule: The east side of Lordsburg: the town's streets (within 250 m of Census TIGER local streets) east of the town's centre point. Today's town is larger than the town of the 1940s.

properties.name: Camp on the alkali flats
properties.reasoning: They camp on alkali flats the text puts fifteen miles west of Lordsburg, burning fenceposts. Fifteen miles due west of Lordsburg (pyproj, WGS 84) falls on the playa west of town; the area allows for the direction.
properties.outline_rule: The alkali flats: the flat ground (slope under 1.5 degrees) joined to the stop, which drops the hills in the south-west. The DEM cannot tell alkali from grass, so the whole flat stays.

properties.name: Noon at the San Simon River
properties.reasoning: They cross a low range and descend into the San Simon Valley where it comes down from the north, and noon at the river under cottonwoods. GNIS pins the valley 54 km north of Bowie, so the stop is a point on the San Simon River between the state line and San Simon town (see the place's reasoning). The pin is on the river itself (NHD).
properties.outline_rule: At the river: within 1 km of the San Simon River (NHD flowline). Where along the river is the circle's estimate.

properties.name: Across the highway east of Bowie
properties.reasoning: That evening they cross the highway just past Bowie, on its east side, and pick up an old southbound road into the Dos Cabezas.
properties.outline_rule: At the highway crossing, east of Bowie: within 1 km of the highway (Census TIGER primary and secondary roads) and east of the town's centre point.

properties.name: The eastern rim of the escarpment at sunrise
properties.reasoning: From Bacerac a rough trail climbs through pine and scrub oak; the next morning, within an hour of setting out, they reach the eastern rim of the escarpment and watch the sun come up over the plains of Chihuahua. The book names no pass; the area is on the eastern edge of the sierra on the line from Bacerac to Colonia Juárez (82.4 km apart).
properties.outline_rule: The eastern rim: ground that looks down at least 300 m within 10 km to the east, within 8 km of the line from Bacerac to Colonia Juárez.

properties.name: The plains, with the Tarahumaras
properties.reasoning: Below the rim they cross prairie to a ciénega where Tarahumaras afoot are watering, headed back into the sierras. The area covers the plain between the escarpment and Colonia Juárez.

properties.name: The girl, at a fire in an oak grove
properties.reasoning: Riding south on the road toward San Diego they see a fire in a grove of oaks east of the road, where two men hold the girl; Boyd stampedes their horses. The area is east of the road between Casas Grandes and San Diego (15.8 km apart).
properties.outline_rule: East of the road: east of the straight line from Casas Grandes to the Hacienda de San Diego (no map of the old road is to hand) and within 3 km of it, where a fire can be seen from the road.

properties.name: The opera company stranded on the Madera road
properties.reasoning: Late in the day they come on the troupe's wagons halted in a roadside field on the Madera road, a few miles below Las Varas, with a dead mule on the road nearby. The estimate is centred 5 km (about three miles) from Las Varas toward Madera, on the bearing between the two towns (200 degrees, pyproj, WGS 84).
properties.outline_rule: A roadside field on the Madera road: within 2 km of the line from Las Varas to Madera (the road is not mapped here) on ground flatter than 4 degrees.

properties.name: Camps by the river
properties.reasoning: They camp in an oak grove by a river, then leave the dirt road for a path past a pepper field and an irrigation ditch to a ford where boys are swimming. The book names neither the river nor a town; the area covers the country along the road between the opera camp and Madera.
properties.outline_rule: By a river near the road: within 1 km of INEGI streams of order 4 and up, and within 4 km of the line from Las Varas to Madera. The book names neither the river nor the road.

properties.name: Crossing of the old wagon road to Namiquipa
properties.reasoning: After three days' riding they reach the crossing of the old wagon road that runs from La Norteña in the western sierras across the Babícora plains and the Santa María valley to Namiquipa. Next morning the girl rides away east toward Namiquipa, which is 57 km due east of the estimate (bearing 92 degrees). The book's compass does not close here: the brothers then ride south into pinewoods and reach Las Varas, which lies to the north, two days later. The area is wide for that reason.
properties.outline_rule: On the wagon road: within 8 km of the line La Norteña, La Babícora, Namiquipa, the road's ends and middle as the book gives them. The book's compass does not close here, so the band is wide.

properties.name: The steer herd on the road to Boquilla
properties.reasoning: In the evening, on the road east to Boquilla, they meet about a thousand steers being trailed from La Quemada to the pens at Naco; after dark they pass a hamlet of log houses on the high plain. The area is on the road between Las Varas and the Babícora lake.
properties.outline_rule: On the road east to Boquilla: within 3 km of the line from Las Varas to La Boquilla.

properties.name: Their horses, up from the lake
properties.reasoning: Next morning two young vaqueros drive their own horses up from a high-country laguna south of the road, and the brothers rope Niño and Bailey. The laguna is the Babícora lake (GeoNames 4017246, 29.35 N, 107.83 W); the area is on the road north of it, and the pin on the line of the road (a straight line from Las Varas to La Boquilla stands in for the old road).
properties.outline_rule: On the road, with the lake to the south: within 2.5 km of the line from Las Varas to La Boquilla, north of the lake and not in it.

properties.name: The manco's riders, the Boquilla hacienda in sight
properties.reasoning: At noon, with the walls of the hacienda in the distance and the lake to the south, riders led by a one-armed man block the road and take the horses. The area is on the road west of La Boquilla, east of the lake.
properties.outline_rule: On the road west of La Boquilla, east of the lake: within 2.5 km of the line from Las Varas to La Boquilla, west of the town and out of the lake.

properties.name: Following the horses' tracks north
properties.reasoning: They ride back west for an hour to where the tracks leave the road above the lake and follow them north all afternoon, sighting the riders at twilight, and camp in a swale. The area is north of the lake.

properties.name: Quijada's remuda
properties.reasoning: Next day they reach an east-west road, follow it east to a crossroads where a track comes down from the mountains to the north, and Quijada, superintendent of the Nahuerichic division, leads them up the road to the remuda and lets Boyd cut out three horses. The book gives no distances; the area is north-east of the tracking camp.

properties.name: Off the road north of Boquilla, west to a river
properties.reasoning: About a mile above the town they turn off the road and head west to a river with nine horses, turning the Boquilla horses back. The book does not name the river; the area is north-west of La Boquilla.
properties.outline_rule: Between the road north of Boquilla and the river to its west: west of La Boquilla and north of the lake. They leave the road a mile above the town and ride west to a river (3-08).

properties.name: The dry camp after the night ride
properties.reasoning: They cross the river upcountry, ride all night through open country away from it, and make a dry camp toward morning in a burned grove on a rise a mile west of the river. The area is between Boquilla and San José, which are 48 km apart (bearing 340 degrees).

properties.name: The river camp where Boyd is shot
properties.reasoning: They camp in a cottonwood grove by the river near San José. At dawn five riders come upriver on the far bank and Boyd is shot from across the river. The book gives no distance from the pueblito; the area is around it.
properties.outline_rule: By the river: within 800 m of the stream nearest San José (INEGI, order 4 and up). The camp is in a cottonwood grove by the river and Boyd is shot from the far bank.

properties.name: The road where the workers' truck takes Boyd
properties.reasoning: Billy rides double with Boyd into open country, sees a vehicle crossing in the distance, and on the dirt road meets a flatbed truck of farmworkers coming from the south; they lift Boyd aboard and it goes on north. The area is between the river camp and the main road north to Mata Ortiz.

properties.name: The blind man's house
properties.reasoning: Alone, Billy leads his horse up an arroyo, sees a light far to the north at dusk and goes toward it; near midnight he reaches a fence, turns east to a gate and rides up a clay track to a lone house, where the blind man and his wife take him in. The area is north of the shooting, about a day and a half south of Mata Ortiz by the text's timing.

properties.name: The desert crossroads on the main road north
properties.reasoning: Next morning he rides north along the road and before noon strikes the main road north to Casas Grandes at an empty desert crossroads; he sleeps in a field near the river breaks and rides on in rain. The area is on the road south of Mata Ortiz.
properties.outline_rule: Near the river breaks: within 4 km of the main river (INEGI streams of order 7). He meets the main road north at a crossroads and sleeps in a field near the river breaks.

properties.name: Within earshot of the Las Varas crossing
properties.reasoning: He rides all day, meets the workers' truck in the evening, and in the night hears a train whistle for the crossing at Las Varas. The area is north-east of Las Varas, on the way to Boquilla.
properties.outline_rule: Within earshot of the crossing: within 15 km of Las Varas, a generous reach for a train whistle at night.

properties.name: A stream of the Santa María headwaters
properties.reasoning: An hour along the road west he sleeps beside a stream, one of the Santa María's headwaters, and in the morning the girl rides past on his mother's old horse. The estimate is centred 4 km west of Santa Ana. The real Namiquipa lies north-north-east, not west (see docs/open-questions.md).
properties.outline_rule: Beside a stream: within 1 km of INEGI streams of order 3 and up (the Santa María headwaters on this valley floor).

properties.name: Camp at the edge of the lake
properties.reasoning: They ride on west into the dark and camp at the edge of the lake. The point is on the north-west shore of the Babícora lake (GeoNames 4017246), on INEGI's outline of it, on the way to Las Varas.
properties.outline_rule: The lake's edge: from 500 m inside INEGI's outline of the Babícora lake to 2 km outside it. The shore moves with the water level.

properties.name: Camp on the river south of Mata Ortiz
properties.reasoning: They take the road north by the railroad; the ride to San Diego takes three days, and the last night they stop for the night on a gravel bar by the river, several miles below Mata Ortiz, as cranes pass over heading south. The area is about 9 km south of Mata Ortiz on the river.
properties.outline_rule: On the river: within 600 m of the main river by Mata Ortiz (the INEGI stream nearest the stop, order 5 and up). A gravel bar by the river; 'below Mata Ortiz' could also mean downstream (north).

properties.name: Álamo
properties.reasoning: He passes back north through the mesa hamlets of Álamo and Galeana, places he had come through before. Which Álamo is unresolved (docs/open-questions.md): the estimate is GeoNames 4018952, 15 km south-west of San Buenaventura, and the area covers El Álamo north-east of the town too.

properties.name: Boyd lifted onto the workers' truck
properties.reasoning: Billy sees the farmworkers lift Boyd onto their truck, which goes on north (3-08); from here Boyd's road is known only from what others tell Billy. The area is the same as J4's.

properties.name: The shallow salt lake
properties.reasoning: At sunset he reaches a shallow salt lake his horse will not cross, rides south along the flats with snow on Gillespie Mountain and the Animas Peaks beyond, and camps by an old fence. The lake is Playas Lake (GNIS 893357, 31.88 N, 108.59 W), the salt flat west of the Little Hatchets; the area is its southern end.
properties.outline_rule: The lake bed and its flats: ground within 8 m of the lowest ground in the circle (Playas Lake's floor). He rides south along the flats and camps by a fence.

properties.name: The old Playas road over the mountains
properties.reasoning: In the morning they cross the lake, strike the old Playas road before noon and follow it west into the mountains, with snow in the pass. The book does not name the pass; the area is in the Animas Mountains west of the lake.
properties.outline_rule: In the mountains on a road: ground above 1,450 m within 2 km of Census TIGER roads. The old Playas road crosses the range with snow in the pass; which road is not known.

properties.name: Sanders' (the SK Bar)
properties.reasoning: He reaches the Sanders ranch two hours after dark, eats supper and will not stay the night. In 4-02 it is called the SK Bar. No source names the ranch (docs/open-questions.md); the estimate is the same as J3's, nine miles north of the Parham house.
properties.outline_rule: The ranch house is on the road: within 2.5 km of the road north from Cloverdale (today's State Highway 338 and Cloverdale Road, Census TIGER). The book gives nine miles by road from the Parham house, so the circle still fixes where along the road.

properties.name: Camp on the Animas Plain
properties.reasoning: That night's camp is out on the wide Animas Plain, with lightning showing in the far south past the Hatchet Mountains. The area is on the open plain south-east of the Sanders estimate.
properties.outline_rule: The open plain: the Animas Valley floor below 1,650 m with a slope under 2 degrees, the part joined to the stop.

properties.name: The SK Bar gate
properties.reasoning: Two days later he reaches the SK Bar gate, learns that Miller died on Kwajalein, and stays the night in the rain. The estimate is J3's (docs/open-questions.md).
properties.outline_rule: The ranch house is on the road: within 2.5 km of the road north from Cloverdale (today's State Highway 338 and Cloverdale Road, Census TIGER). The book gives nine miles by road from the Parham house, so the circle still fixes where along the road.

properties.name: Camp on the plain by the lake, the red plane
properties.reasoning: On the road east toward La Boquilla a north wind blows dust off Babícora beyond the lake, a red plane flies in from the west, and he camps on the plain. The area is north-east of the Babícora lake. The pin is on the flat ground by the road.
properties.outline_rule: On the plain by the road: ground flatter than 2 degrees within 4 km of the line from Las Varas to La Boquilla, out of the lake.

properties.name: The high country of the Babícora
properties.reasoning: For days he camps in the swales of the Babícora high country and watches vaqueros working whiteface cattle on mules. The area covers the plains around the lake and the ranch headquarters.
properties.outline_rule: The plains around the lake: ground below 2,250 m with a slope under 4 degrees (the Babícora basin floor and its swales), lake included.

properties.name: Quijada's cabin
properties.reasoning: One evening he follows a road west toward a gap in the mountains and after dark reaches a lone weatherboard cabin on the plain, where Quijada, still manager of the Nahuerichic division, tells him where Boyd fell and lies. Next day he rides north all day to San Buenaventura, so the area is about a day's ride (47 km) south-south-west of it. It is 57 km from Nahuerachi, the open-questions pick for the division's name.
properties.outline_rule: On the plain: ground with a slope under 3 degrees. The cabin is a lone house on the plain on a road toward a gap in the mountains.

properties.name: Boyd's grave, on the Gallego road
properties.reasoning: The cemetery is on a bench in the low hills east of town, a mile or so up the old road to Gallego, with the Sierra del Nido in sight. He finds the board cross by the south wall and digs all day. The estimate is centred 1.6 km due east of the town point.

properties.name: Past the lights of Casas Grandes, to the west
properties.reasoning: Near midnight he leaves with the bones on the packhorse, crosses the highway and heads across country with the polestar to his right. In two nights' riding he sees the lights of Casas Grandes to the west of him, so he is east of the town; the area is 15 km east of it.
properties.outline_rule: Where the town's lights show: ground in sight of a light 10 m up at Nuevo Casas Grandes (viewshed of the 30 m DEM, eye at 2 m) and east of the town.

properties.name: The Casas Grandes River, across the Guzmán road
properties.reasoning: He crosses the old road that runs down from Guzmán and Sabinal, reaches the Casas Grandes River and follows a trail north beside it. The area is on the river south of Corralitos, and the pin on the river itself (INEGI).
properties.outline_rule: At the river: within 1 km of the Casas Grandes River (the INEGI stream nearest Corralitos, order 6). He reaches the river and follows a trail north beside it.

properties.name: The attack on the river trail, and the gypsies' camp
properties.reasoning: An hour north of the town four riders stop him on the trail, cut open the bones and stab Niño; the next day gypsies hauling an old airplane north camp with him by the river and doctor the horse (4-06, 4-07). An hour's ride is about 6 km; the pin is on the river trail beside the Casas Grandes River (INEGI), 7.3 km north of Corralitos (pyproj, WGS 84).
properties.outline_rule: On the river trail: within 1 km of the Casas Grandes River (INEGI, order 6).

properties.name: The border, west of Dog Springs
properties.reasoning: Four days later he sets out north along the river with the bones on a travois; it takes three days to reach the border, where he passes the first boundary obelisk west of Dog Springs and an old dry reservoir. No Dog Springs is known on the line (docs/open-questions.md); the estimate is the boundary south of Hermanas.
properties.outline_rule: At the boundary: within 1.5 km of the line along 31°47′ N. He passes an obelisk on the line; where along it is the circle's estimate.

properties.name: The little cemetery south of Animas
properties.reasoning: He buys a spade and goes south from the town to a little cemetery, where he buries Boyd; the sheriff tells him to report at Lordsburg. GNIS lists no cemetery here; the area is just south of the town.
properties.outline_rule: South of the town: the circle south of Animas's centre point.

properties.name: Over the Black Range
properties.reasoning: He crosses the Black Range on the old road east. The book names no pass; the road from San Lorenzo crosses the range at Emory Pass (GNIS 906157), where the estimate is centred.
properties.outline_rule: On the road over the pass: within 1 km of NM 152 (Census TIGER), the old road east over Emory Pass.

properties.name: The ruined waystation by the blacktop
properties.reasoning: Beyond the range he crosses a plain of catclaw and creosote, strikes the blacktop a few miles on, sees the Organ Mountains about eighty miles off, and turns back along the highway to three ruined adobes with a rusted gas pump, once a waystation. There he drives off the crippled dog, and wakes to the false dawn (4-09). The area is on the plain east of Hillsboro; the pin, by the highway, is 113 km (70 miles) straight-line from the Organ Mountains point (GNIS 920657, pyproj, WGS 84), and Emory Pass is 131 km (81 miles), so the book's eighty miles fits the range's eastern foot.
properties.outline_rule: By the blacktop: within 500 m of the highways in the circle (Census TIGER secondary roads, NM 152 and NM 27). The waystation's adobes stand by the highway.

properties.name: The Animas Valley
properties.reasoning: The valley floor between the Animas and Peloncillo ranges, where the wolf runs and the Parhams live (Part I) and the text's Animas Plain lies (2-04, 4-02). Drafted from the DEM as the ground below 1,600 m connected to J1's Animas Valley stop, between the border and Animas town; the ranges on either side rise above 1,800 m. To be checked by hand in QGIS (decision 0008).

properties.name: La Babícora
properties.reasoning: The plains of the Babícora, Hearst's ranch country, named at Casas Grandes (2-08) and ridden by Billy in Part IV. Drafted from the DEM as the basin floor below 2,200 m connected to the hacienda's pin, around the Laguna de Babícora; the estate's legal bounds are not known to this project. To be checked by hand in QGIS (decision 0008).
